title: Deploy a FastAPI App to the Cloud
description: Deploy a Python FastAPI application to a free cloud platform with environment variables and a live URL
objective: Students will take a FastAPI application, prepare it for deployment with requirements.txt and environment variables, deploy to a free cloud platform, and verify the live API works

steps.title: Prepare the Project for Deployment
steps.instructions:
Make sure your FastAPI project has these files:

`main.py` — your API code

`requirements.txt` — create with:
```bash
pip freeze > requirements.txt
```

Or manually:
```
fastapi==0.115.0
uvicorn==0.30.0
python-dotenv==1.0.0
```

`.env` — environment variables (local only):
```
SECRET_KEY=my-local-secret
DEBUG=true
```

`.gitignore` — exclude sensitive files:
```
.env
__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.db
venv/
```

Update `main.py` to use environment variables:
```python
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

DEBUG = os.getenv("DEBUG", "false") == "true"
SECRET = os.getenv("SECRET_KEY", "default-key")
```

Test locally: `uvicorn main:app --reload`

steps.title: Push to GitHub
steps.instructions:
If not already a Git repo:
```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Prepare for deployment"
```

Create a new GitHub repository and push:
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/student-api.git
git push -u origin main
```

Verify on GitHub:
- `main.py` is there
- `requirements.txt` is there
- `.env` is NOT there (should be in .gitignore)
- No `__pycache__` or `.pyc` files

steps.title: Deploy to Render (Free)
steps.instructions:
1. Go to https://render.com/ and sign up with GitHub
2. Click **New** → **Web Service**
3. Connect your GitHub repository
4. Configure:
   - **Name:** student-api
   - **Runtime:** Python 3
   - **Build Command:** `pip install -r requirements.txt`
   - **Start Command:** `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
   - **Plan:** Free

5. Add Environment Variables:
   - Click **Environment** → **Add Environment Variable**
   - `SECRET_KEY` = `your-production-secret-here`
   - `DEBUG` = `false`

6. Click **Create Web Service**

Wait for the build to complete (2-5 minutes).

Your API will be live at: `https://student-api-xxxx.onrender.com`

Test the live URL:
- `/` — should return JSON message
- `/docs` — should show Swagger UI
- `/api/students` — should return student data

steps.title: Verify and Test the Live API
steps.instructions:
Open your live URL in the browser and test:

| URL | Expected |
|-----|----------|
| `https://your-app.onrender.com/` | JSON welcome message |
| `https://your-app.onrender.com/docs` | Swagger UI loads |
| `https://your-app.onrender.com/api/students` | Student list |

Test with Postman or curl:
```bash
curl https://your-app.onrender.com/api/students
```

Test a POST request (from Swagger UI or Postman):
```json
{
  "name": "Test Student",
  "email": "test@email.com",
  "course": "ADCA",
  "marks": 80,
  "city": "Bhopal"
}
```

Note: On free Render, the app sleeps after inactivity. First request after sleep takes ~30 seconds.

Update your README with the live URL:
```markdown
## Live Demo
API: https://your-app.onrender.com
Docs: https://your-app.onrender.com/docs
```

Commit and push the updated README.

steps.title: Monitor and Troubleshoot
steps.instructions:
Check for common deployment issues:

**If the app won't start:**
- Check build logs on Render dashboard for errors
- Make sure `requirements.txt` has all packages
- Verify the start command is correct: `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`

**If API returns errors:**
- Check if environment variables are set correctly
- Test locally first: `uvicorn main:app --reload`
- Look at Render logs for Python tracebacks

**Performance check:**
- Open Chrome DevTools → Network tab
- Load your API endpoint
- Check response time (should be under 500ms after wake-up)

**Auto-deploy test:**
1. Make a small change locally (update the welcome message)
2. Commit and push:
```bash
git add main.py
git commit -m "Update welcome message"
git push
```
3. Watch Render dashboard — it should auto-deploy
4. After deploy completes, refresh your live URL — the change should be live

This is how real production deployment works: push to GitHub → auto-deploy → live.

**Submit:** GitHub repo link + live deployed URL + screenshot of Swagger UI + screenshot of Render build logs.

expected_output: A FastAPI application deployed to Render with a live URL, environment variables configured, Swagger docs accessible, and API endpoints responding correctly
